Dashed line takes up to three Dash and Gap pairs (a Gap left empty takes the dash value); with Preserve exact dash and gap lengths and no arrowhead the pairs are written straight to stroke-dasharray on the path. Align dashes to corners and path ends, adjusting lengths to fit, or any arrowhead, wraps the path in a g carrying data-fw-stroke (10 keys: v, src, dash, mode, a0, a1, s0, s1, tip, sig) with the source path kept editable (stroke-opacity 0, so colour, weight, cap and join still come from it) and one generated group data-fw-live=stroke that liveFixes regenerates when the path or the settings change. Align mode splits the stroke at corners (anchors where the tangent turns by more than 2 degrees) and at path ends, and gives each run a stroke-dasharray scaled by L / (n * period) with n = round(L / period) and a stroke-dashoffset of half the first dash, so a dash is centred on every corner and end. Arrowheads (none, simple arrow, filled triangle, open triangle, circle, square, bar) are generated paths oriented by the end tangent and coloured with the stroke, scaled per end in percent of 4 times the weight, with Extend arrow tip beyond end of path (base at the end point) or Place arrow tip at end of path (tip at the end point and the body trimmed by the head length). Remove dashes and arrowheads restores the plain stroke; Expand turns the generated paths into ordinary ones; a Width tool button opens the Width tool. vector.rs validates data-fw-stroke (dash at most six non-negative numbers in pairs, enums, scale 1 to 1000, src a non-generated path child of the group). Driven in headless Chromium against the real engine and read from GET /api/state: dash 12 12, then 10 with an empty gap (stored 10 10), two pairs (10 10 4 8) and three pairs (10 10 4 8 2 3); Align on a three segment zigzag gave three parts with dasharray scaled by 0.954 and dashoffset 4.774; Align on a rectangle gave four parts; a filled start and open end arrowhead with tip at end trimmed both ends by 16 units and put the tips on the end points; circle and bar heads; dragging an end anchor regenerated the body and the heads; Remove returned one plain path with its stroke. Three changes dispatched in one synchronous script (dash 9, end arrowhead filled triangle, scale end 150) were queued and all landed in one spec. Caps (Butt, Round, Projecting stored as square), joins (Miter, Round, Bevel) and Miter limit were driven in the same pass. v0.8.6: Align mode no longer writes a dasharray per run; it cuts dashes by arc length (scaled per run, centred on every corner and end) and merges the two half dashes at a corner into one open sub-path spanning the corner, so the path's line join applies; one generated path per sub-path holds all dashes. Driven on a four anchor zigzag at weight 12: the corner dashes read M119.16 7.68 L122.91 3 L126.66 7.68 and M239.06 148.2 L242.81 152.88 L246.56 148.2 in GET /api/state, and the screenshot shows V shaped dashes at the corners. Generated parts now honour stroke align: a rectangle with weight 1 and Inside gave parts with stroke-width 2 and the source's clip-path url(#fwa-...); Outside on a filled rectangle moved the generated group under the source so the fill covers the inner half (as paint-order stroke does for plain strokes), the clip is regenerated when align changes and Center removed it; arrowheads on an open path with Inside carried the same clip-path and doubled width on stroked heads; Expand kept the shared clipPath so expanded parts stay clipped. A path with a variable width can now be dashed and arrowed: the outline is cut along the path length into filled ribbon pieces with the profile, cap, line join and miter limit (Bulge on a zigzag gave 24 dash pieces in one fill path coloured as the width, Align gave 25 with V shaped corner pieces; a rectangle with width points dragged in the Width tool gave 41 and, aligned, 40); heads are sized by the width at the ends (Taper both gave the 1 unit minimum, Bulge 5.6) and Place arrow tip trims the body by that head length; the width outline sibling is hidden with opacity 0 while the stroke group exists and restored by Remove; dragging an anchor, a Width tool drag, undo and Remove were driven and regenerated or restored the parts.

Aligned dashes at a corner use the miter, round or bevel join of the path, but in a variable width path the join is built on the offset ribbon, not by the browser stroker; the arrowhead set and its size (4 times the weight at 100 percent) are FormWeb's own and not Illustrator's; heads are not drawn on closed paths; arrowheads on an open path with Inside or Outside align are clipped to the implicitly closed region like the plain stroke, where Illustrator disables those modes for open paths; align is not applied to a variable width path (the existing Width tool behaviour); Preserve with a variable width and no arrowhead still produces filled pieces, not a stroke-dasharray; the secondary sources give no exact labels, defaults or ranges, so those were not matched.
